title: Assignment: vectors, prefix sums & patterns
overview: This module is an assignment that checks the tools from modules 1 to 3. You find duplicates by sorting, print a prefix-sum array backwards, check if arrays are sorted, insert one vector into another, and draw an X pattern. Each solution is a short, typical judge program.

concepts.explain: After sorting, equal values sit next to each other, so one pass comparing `A[i]` with `A[i-1]` finds any duplicate.
Values up to 10^9 add up past the `int` limit quickly, so the running sum must be `long long`.
An array is sorted ascending if no element is smaller than the one before it. One broken pair is enough to answer NO.
`A.insert(A.begin() + X, value)` puts a value at index `X` and shifts the rest right. Increase `X` after each insert to keep the inserted block in order.
For each row, work out how many spaces come before, between and after the characters, and how those counts change from row to row.
Read `T` first, then repeat the whole read-solve-print routine `T` times, resetting variables inside the loop.

files.title: Duplicate
files.what: Prints YES if any value appears twice. It sorts the vector and compares neighbours.
steps: `sort` it so equal values become neighbours.
For `i` from 1, if `A[i] == A[i-1]`, print `YES` and exit.
files.complexity: Time O(n log n) · Space O(n)
files.output_note: `YES`: after sorting (`1 1 2 2 3 5`) the first two values are equal.

check.q: Why is a frequency array a bad idea here?
check.a: Values go up to 10^9, far too large for an array index.

files.title: Get prefix sum (reversed)
files.what: Builds the prefix-sum array with `long long` and prints it from the last position to the first.
steps: Read the values into `vector<long long> nums`.
files.input_note: n, then n numbers (this case tests overflow).
files.output_note: `3000000000 2000000000 1000000000`: the totals are larger than an `int` can hold, and they print correctly because of `long long`.

check.q: What would this sample print if the sums were `int`?

files.title: Sorted
files.what: For each test case, prints YES if the array is in non-decreasing order, else NO.
steps: Start `flag = true`; if any `A[j] < A[j-1]`, set it false and `break`.
files.complexity: Time O(N) per test · Space O(N)
files.input_note: T, then for each test: N and the array.
files.output_note: `YES` (strictly rising), `YES` (equal neighbours are allowed), `NO` (1 comes after 100).

check.q: Why use `<` and not `<=` in the comparison?
check.a: Equal neighbours still count as sorted ascending, so only a strict drop breaks the order.

files.title: Insert it
files.what: Inserts every element of B into A starting at index X, keeping B's order, then prints A.
steps: Then `X++`, so the next element goes right after the one just inserted.
files.complexity: Time O(M * (N + M)) · Space O(N + M)
files.input_note: N, A, M, B, then X.
files.output_note: `2 3 4 10 20 30 5 6`: B sits in the middle, starting at index 3.
files.watch_out: Without `X++`, B would end up reversed (`30 20 10`). One call `A.insert(A.begin() + X, B.begin(), B.end());` does the whole job in O(N + M).

check.q: What does the program print for X = 0 with the same arrays?

files.title: Printing X
files.what: Draws an X of height `N` (odd) with `\` and `/`, putting `X` in the middle row.
steps: Top half (`N/2` rows): row `i` has `i` spaces, `\`, `spaces` gaps, `/`, and `i` spaces. `spaces` starts at `N-2` and drops by 2 each row.
Bottom half: `space_before_after` starts at `N/2 - 1` and shrinks by 1; `space_between` starts at 1 and grows by 2; each row prints `/`, the gap, `\`.
files.output_note: A 7-line X: the arms meet at the `X` in row 4. In the top half the gap between `\` and `/` shrinks 5, 3, 1; in the bottom half it grows 1, 3, 5.
files.watch_out: The middle row has no trailing spaces while the other rows do. Most judges ignore trailing spaces, but a strict checker would not. Remember `\` in a C++ string prints one backslash.

check.q: How many spaces are between the slashes on the first row when N = 9?

recap: Sort first when you need to spot equal values.
Use `long long` for any running total of large numbers.
An array is sorted if no neighbour pair goes down.
Increase the insert position after each `insert` to keep the inserted block's order.
Pattern problems: write down the space counts per row, then find how they change.

check_yourself.q: How can you check for duplicates in O(n) average time without sorting?
check_yourself.a: Insert values into an `unordered_set` and report YES when an insert finds the value already present.

check_yourself.q: What is the time complexity of inserting M elements one by one at the front of a vector of size N?
check_yourself.a: O(M * (N + M)), because each insert shifts every element after it.
